channel.title: Kubai Kevin
channel.description: Practical backend engineering, AI tooling, and developer career advice by Kubai Kevin — a software developer with 10+ years building production systems in fintech and AI.

item.title: Node.js memory leak: find it in 10 min
item.description: Classify rising memory before profiling it: compare heapUsed and rss, take two heap snapshots, read retainer paths, and bound every in-memory structure.

item.title: AI answers first, judgment later
item.description: AI assistants give juniors fast, confident answers without your system's context. Here is how to move mentoring from giving answers to reviewing judgment.

item.title: Database restore drills that mean something
item.description: A repeatable PostgreSQL restore drill that measures recovery time, data loss window and integrity, plus the failure modes that make drills lie.

item.title: Multi-agent DX: LangGraph vs CrewAI gaps
item.description: Where LangGraph and CrewAI leave you on your own when debugging multi-agent systems, the failure modes that recur, and how to instrument for causal traces.

item.title: JWT sessions: revocation, rotation, storage
item.description: Why JWT revocation is a state problem, how refresh token rotation with reuse detection works, and how token storage shapes the threat model.

item.title: Context engineering: the real fix for agent hallucinations
item.description: Long-running agents fail because their context fills with stale tool output and contradictions. Here is how to structure, prune and measure that context.

item.title: HPA vs KEDA vs Karpenter: autoscaling traps
item.description: How HPA, KEDA and Karpenter divide responsibility, where each one silently fails, and how to verify each layer before traffic arrives.

item.title: Drift detection: the plan that lies
item.description: Terraform plan only reports drift a provider reads back. Build observe-classify-remediate pipelines that catch out-of-band changes safely.

item.title: 7 guardrails for safer LLM apps
item.description: A practical review of seven guardrail layers for LLM applications: what each catches, where it fails, and which to build first.

item.title: When velocity is hard to measure: evaluating engineering…
item.description: Velocity measures capacity, not output. Build a three-layer evidence portfolio—delivery, stability, outcome—and compute it from data you already have.

item.title: ISO 20022: where payment rails actually break
item.description: ISO 20022 migrations fail in mapping policy, code-list governance and character rules, not XML parsing. A layered design and checklist for payment rails.

item.title: HTTP/3 changes less than the demos imply
item.description: HTTP/3 usually terminates at the CDN, so origin behavior barely changes. Here is where QUIC matters, where it does not, and how to measure a rollout.

item.title: Agentic systems: architecture principles that hold
item.description: How to enforce deadlines, token budgets, idempotency keys and bounded fan-out around multi-model agent graphs, with Python code and tests.

item.title: Agent code review: 7 traps that slip through
item.description: Agent-written code passes its own tests and reads as deliberate. Here are seven recurring traps, the mechanical checks that catch them, and how to measure.

item.title: OAuth 2.1 migration: what breaks in existing integrations
item.description: OAuth 2.1 removes the implicit and password grants, mandates PKCE, and requires exact redirect URIs. Here is what breaks and how to sequence the migration.

item.title: Velocity Up, Ownership Down: Team Scaling Trap
item.description: A practical framework for finding ownership blur, assigning accountable owners, and enforcing it with CODEOWNERS, CI checks, and incident tooling.

item.title: Remote premium rates: skills AI can't copy
item.description: Four drills for remote engineers: latency budgets, evidence-based diagnosis, decision records and handoff artifacts that outlast the work.

item.title: Docs that survive: the bus factor fix
item.description: How to write runbooks and design docs that a new engineer can follow without asking the author: explicit audience, exact commands, expected output, and rollback.

item.title: MCP vs A2A: pick the wrong layer
item.description: MCP connects models to tools; A2A connects agents to agents. How to tell which layer a boundary belongs to, and what breaks when you mix them.

item.title: Property-based testing vs example tests: the bug gap
item.description: How example-based and property-based tests differ in what they catch, what each costs to maintain, and how to split work between them in financial code.
